claims.explanation: SDM25N is an opioid receptor antagonist that also inhibits dengue virus replication by targeting the viral NS4B protein, but in cancer cells its selectivity may be driven by modulation of opioid receptor signaling, particularly through OPRD1 (delta-opioid receptor). The pattern of sensitive lines suggests that co-occurring mutations in TP53 and KRAS, along with alterations in chromatin modifiers (e.g., KMT2C/D, ARID1A, EP300), may sensitize cells to SDM25N, while mutations in PTEN, BRAF, or EGFR are associated with resistance. The drug's known antiviral activity via NS4B is unlikely to explain anticancer selectivity, so the opioid receptor pathway and downstream signaling interactions with oncogenic drivers are more plausible.

features.basis: TP53 mutations are highly enriched in sensitive lines (e.g., T3M4, HEC265, KALS1) and less common in resistant lines, suggesting loss of p53 function may enhance sensitivity to SDM25N.
KRAS mutations appear in several sensitive lines (T3M4, OV7, CL11) but are absent in many resistant lines, indicating a potential association with sensitivity.
PTEN mutations are frequent in resistant lines (ZR751, UACC62, SNU840) and rare in sensitive lines, suggesting PTEN loss may confer resistance.
BRAF mutations are common in resistant melanoma lines (UACC62, K029AX, IPC298) and appear in some sensitive lines, but overall association with resistance is stronger.
EGFR mutations are present in resistant lung lines (NCIH1650, KYSE270) and in one sensitive line (HCC4006), but the resistant pattern suggests a protective role.
SDM25N is a delta-opioid receptor antagonist; expression of OPRD1 may mediate its anticancer effects, though direct evidence is lacking.
KMT2C mutations appear in multiple sensitive lines (T3M4, FTC133, OV7) but also in some resistant lines, suggesting a possible but weaker association.
ARID1A mutations are found in sensitive lines (HEC265, LOXIMVI) but also in resistant lines, indicating a complex role.
NF1 mutations appear in sensitive lines (KALS1, FTC133, LOXIMVI, BICR6) but also in resistant lines, suggesting a potential but not definitive link.
PIK3CA mutations are present in resistant lines (SNU840, KYSE510, SNUC5) and in some sensitive lines, but the resistant association is notable.
CDKN2A mutations appear in resistant lines (K029AX, IPC298) and in one sensitive line (MHHES1), suggesting a possible protective role.
ATM mutations are found in resistant lines (SNU685, SNUC5) and in one sensitive line (786O), indicating a potential association with resistance.
